description: Production container baseline. The image was never measured or scanned by any workflow before this initiative.
establishedBy: PR CI run 19 (run id 30431556718), job `container-security / container-security`, artifact `evidence-container-security`, file `image-metadata.json`, at feature head 8d7bfff09cf914e00ff5ff4587341ece261185c3, started 2026-07-29T07:24:48Z, GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest.
establishmentNote: Recorded from the first GitHub-hosted container job that ever measured the image. The ratchet starts from the run after this one.
imageSizeKind: UNCOMPRESSED on-disk size, from `docker image inspect --format '{{.Size}}'` (193.5 MiB across 12 layers). This is NOT the compressed size a registry would report. No compressed figure is recorded because the image is built and scanned in-job and never pushed, so no registry manifest exists to measure; `docker save | gzip` was not run. A future release workflow that pushes the image is where a compressed baseline belongs.
imageIdKind: PROVENANCE ONLY — recorded, never enforced, and deliberately not named `imageId` so nobody later mistakes it for a pin. Three reasons it cannot be one: it is a LOCAL image config ID from `docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}'`, not a registry manifest digest (the image is never pushed, so `RepoDigests` is empty); Next.js emits a fresh random build ID into `.next` on every build, so the image content differs run to run even from an identical source tree; and only `imageSizeBytes` is read by the container job. It identifies the exact image this one run built, and that is all.
runtimeIdentityNote: The Dockerfile creates a dedicated `nextjs:nodejs` account at 1001:1001 rather than reusing the image's built-in `node` user (uid 1000), so the application owns nothing it does not need (ADR-007). Asserting the exact value — not merely `uid != 0` — catches a silent change to a different, possibly shared, account.
unfixablePolicy: Findings at a blocking severity with no fixed version available are REPORTED, not blocking. The action for them is to change or rebuild the base image, which is a different decision from bumping a package; conflating the two teaches everyone to ignore the gate. The nightly deep scan drops the `ignore-unfixed` filter so the full picture is always visible.
